secrets_policy: This artifact contains no .env values, no cookie values, no API keys and no password hashes. Secret-bearing lines are cited by file:line only. The real .env (working tree, untracked) was not read for its values; only its existence and file mode were observed.

summary.posture: The hardening pass already applied to this branch is real and verifiable: install lock auto-creation, payment-secret encryption at rest with an APP_KEY-backed cast, secret masking in the admin UI, uploads/storage PHP-execution denial in both nginx configs, dotfile denial, security headers, empty-by-default TRUSTED_PROXIES, admin login rate limiting, forced default-password rotation, installer input validation, and a CSRF exception list limited to payment notify/return callbacks. The residual risk concentrates in (1) unauthenticated installer reachability + destructive install.sql when install.lock is missing, (2) an enabled-by-default 易支付 (yipay) row whose signing key is a documented placeholder, and (3) secret material for system settings (SMTP password, bot tokens) kept in a plaintext Redis cache.
summary.session_cookie_state: http_only=true, same_site=lax, secure=false (explicit in .env.example; config default is null), encrypt=false, lifetime 120m, remember-me enabled for the admin guard.
summary.install_lock_state: Auto-created by the shipped entrypoints when INSTALL != true (Dockerfile:14, conf/start.sh:28-30); the lock is the only gate in front of the installer and is checked before, not during, do-install.

install_lock.gate: app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:16-24 — redirects to '/' when BASE_PATH/install.lock exists, otherwise forwards.
install_lock.lock_creation_installer: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:216 — file_put_contents(BASE_PATH/install.lock, 'install ok', LOCK_EX) executed AFTER .env write (line 202), install.sql import (line 204) and admin row update (lines 206-211).
install_lock.lock_creation_container_debian: Dockerfile:11-17 writes /app/start.sh with `if [ "$INSTALL" != "true" ] && [ ! -e /app/install.lock ]; then echo ok > /app/install.lock; fi` and Dockerfile:4 sets INSTALL=false.
install_lock.lock_creation_container_arm64: conf/start.sh:28-30 (copied by Dockerfile-ARM64:25), same INSTALL gate from Dockerfile-ARM64:6.
install_lock.secondary_gate: app/Http/Middleware/DujiaoBoot.php:19-23 redirects every `dujiaoka.boot` route to /install while the lock file is absent.
install_lock.routes: routes/common/web.php:37-42 — GET /install and POST /do-install are the only two routes in the install.check group; no auth middleware.
install_lock.destructive_payload: database/sql/install.sql contains 21 `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` statements, an admin_users insert (line 246) and an unconditional `UPDATE pays SET is_open = 0` followed by enabling only /pay/yipay (lines 538-540).
notes: The installer rewrites .env wholesale from .env.example (HomeController:184-202), so re-running it replaces DB/Redis credentials and the APP_KEY placeholder with a freshly generated key.
do-install itself does not re-check install.lock, so a race between two concurrent first-install requests is possible (lock is written last).

proxy_trust.config: config/app.php:18 'trusted_proxies' => env('TRUSTED_PROXIES'); .env.example:64-66 documents that it should stay empty unless behind a trusted proxy.
proxy_trust.middleware: app/Http/Middleware/TrustProxies.php:19-35 — $proxies stays null when the env value is empty (trust nothing), otherwise '*' or a comma-separated list; headers include X-Forwarded-For/Host/Port/Proto (line 26).
consequences: Empty value = secure default: client-supplied X-Forwarded-For cannot spoof Request::ip() and therefore cannot rotate the admin-login rate-limit key (AuthController:17).

Empty value behind a TLS-terminating proxy = $request->isSecure() false, so SecurityHeaders.php:20-22 never emits HSTS and the app believes it is on HTTP — ADMIN_HTTPS (config/admin.php:117, .env.example:49) must be set manually.
Setting TRUSTED_PROXIES=* re-enables X-Forwarded-For spoofing, which directly weakens the per-IP login limiter and any IP-keyed throttling.

security_headers.application: app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php:15-22 — X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy camera/microphone/geolocation, HSTS only when $request->isSecure().
security_headers.nginx: conf/default.conf:10-13 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:4-7 duplicate the same four headers with `always`; conf/default.conf:5 / :2 server_tokens off.
gaps: No Content-Security-Policy anywhere (app middleware or nginx).
No HSTS in HTTP-only deployments; HSTS depends on correct proxy trust (above).
X-Frame-Options is SAMEORIGIN rather than DENY; framing by same-origin pages (including any stored HTML/SVG upload) remains possible.

No extension whitelist exists for admin uploads, so an administrator can still place SVG/HTML in a same-origin path (stored-XSS surface, admin-only).

findings.title: Unauthenticated installer can wipe the database and reset the administrator when install.lock is absent

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23 gates only on file_exists(BASE_PATH/install.lock); routes/common/web.php:37-42 expose GET /install and POST /do-install with no auth.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:184-216 writes .env (line 202), imports database/sql/install.sql via DB::unprepared (line 204), overwrites admin_users id=1 with attacker-supplied username/password (lines 206-211) and only then writes install.lock (line 216).
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: database/sql/install.sql contains 21 `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` statements plus `UPDATE pays SET is_open = 0` (lines 538-540) — a successful call destroys existing orders/goods/carmis data and hands over the admin account; POST /do-install is reachable by any network client.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Dockerfile:14 and conf/start.sh:28-30 auto-create install.lock when INSTALL != true, and app/Http/Middleware/DujiaoBoot.php:19-23 forces /install while the file is missing.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: The shipped container entrypoints create install.lock at startup by default (INSTALL=false), so a standard deployment closes the route before any request is served. Exposure requires INSTALL=true (documented first-install mode), a missing/unwritable lock file, a bind-mounted install.lock path that Docker materialises as a directory, or a non-container deployment where the operator follows the manual install README.
preconditions: install.lock absent at request time
POST /do-install reachable from the attacker's network
php process able to write /app/.env and reach the database
findings.recommendation: Make do-install refuse to run when .env already exists or the admin_users table already contains rows; write install.lock before mutating state; require a one-time install token; and re-check the lock inside the controller.

findings.title: 易支付 (yipay) is the only channel enabled by default and its seeded signing key is the public placeholder '密钥'

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: database/sql/install.sql:515-517 seed the three /pay/yipay rows with merchant_pem = the literal placeholder '密钥'; database/sql/install.sql:538-540 (`UPDATE pays SET is_open = 0` then `is_open = 1 WHERE pay_handleroute = '/pay/yipay'`) leave exactly those rows enabled after a fresh install.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:82-96 rebuilds the signature as md5(ksort'ed key=value pairs . $payGateway->merchant_pem) and compares it with hash_equals; merchant_pem is used verbatim as the shared secret.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: routes/common/pay.php:28 exposes GET /pay/yipay/notify_url anonymously (CSRF does not apply to GET). On success app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:101 calls OrderProcessService::completedOrder(), which only cross-checks the amount (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-422) and a unique trade_no (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:411-417) before delivering carmis.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: No startup check refuses to serve a gateway whose merchant_pem/merchant_key still equals a seeded placeholder; app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:89-105 validates only order/pay_id consistency.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Exploitation needs (a) the operator to leave the yipay row untouched (the installer does not prompt for gateway credentials), (b) a known order_sn, which is obtainable from the public buy/order flow, and (c) the attacker to compute md5 over the same parameter set, which is possible because the key is a documented constant. The rival consideration is that an untouched gateway also has an empty merchant_key (form action), so the legitimate payment flow is visibly broken and an attentive operator may notice — but the notify endpoint still verifies. No dynamic proof was produced in this phase.
preconditions: fresh install or upgrade where merchant_pem still equals the seeded placeholder
attacker can obtain a pending order_sn
attacker can send a GET request to /pay/yipay/notify_url
findings.recommendation: Seed gateway rows disabled (is_open=0 for yipay too), refuse to accept notifications when merchant_pem/pay_handleroute matches a seeded placeholder, and require operator-entered credentials before enabling a channel.

findings.title: Fixed bcrypt administrator row ships in install.sql; plaintext unverified but identical across all installs

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: database/sql/install.sql:246 inserts admin_users id=1 'admin' with a constant $2y$10$ hash (value deliberately not reproduced).
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:206-214 overwrites that row during a successful install; app/Admin/Controllers/AuthController.php:35-37 and app/Http/Middleware/ForceAdminPasswordChange.php:36-38 only force a change when the password is exactly 'admin'.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Any deployment that imports install.sql outside the installer path (manual MySQL import, restored dump, installer failure after DB::unprepared at HomeController:204) keeps the fixed row as the only administrator.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Login is rate limited to 5 attempts/60s per username+IP (app/Admin/Controllers/AuthController.php:17-25) and session fixation is blocked by session regeneration (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Controllers/AuthController.php:239).

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: password_verify() against the shipped hash returned false for seven common passwords (admin, 123456, admin123, password, dujiaoka, 12345678, admin888) in PHP 8.3, so the password is not a trivially guessable string; the real install path replaces the row with an operator-chosen >=10 character password.
preconditions: install.sql imported without the installer's admin update
attacker learns or cracks the fixed hash's plaintext
findings.recommendation: Remove the pre-populated admin row from install.sql and create the first administrator only through the installer (or a console command); force rotation for any row whose password predates installation.

findings.title: Session cookie has no Secure flag by default, remember-me is long-lived, and a password change does not invalidate other sessions

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: config/session.php:169 secure = env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE', null) with .env.example:69 SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=false; config/session.php:197 same_site='lax'; config/session.php:182 http_only=true; config/session.php:49 encrypt=false.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43 registers EncryptCookies/StartSession but leaves AuthenticateSession commented out at line 38; config/admin.php:152 enables remember-me for the admin guard; conf/php.ini:8 sets only session.cookie_httponly.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: All admin and storefront sessions: a cookie observed on any plain-HTTP request is replayable, and after an administrator changes the password every previously issued session/token keeps working indefinitely within the 120-minute lifetime (or far longer for the remember cookie).
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: config/admin.php:117 + .env.example:49 default ADMIN_HTTPS=false, so the documented default deployment is HTTP-only; HSTS is only emitted when $request->isSecure() (app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php:20-22) and proxy trust is empty by default (config/app.php:18).

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Cookies are encrypted by EncryptCookies and HttpOnly+SameSite=lax block script access and most cross-site sends; exploitation needs an on-path observer on plain HTTP or a leaked cookie, and the branch documentation tells operators to enable HTTPS and SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE in production.
preconditions: deployment reachable over plain HTTP, or a proxy that terminates TLS without TRUSTED_PROXIES configured
session cookie disclosed by other means (log, referer, shared host) for the invalidation gap
findings.recommendation: Default the effective secure flag to true in production, enable AuthenticateSession, document SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true together with ADMIN_HTTPS=true, and shorten remember-me lifetime.

findings.title: System settings (SMTP password, bot tokens, geetest key) are cached in plaintext in a Redis store that may be unauthenticated

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Admin/Forms/SystemSetting.php:18-24 stores the entire form array (including fields defined at lines 61-95: server_jiang_token, telegram_bot_token, bark_token, qywxbot_key, geetest key, SMTP password) with Cache::put('system-setting', $input) — no encryption, no allow-list.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Service/MailConfigService.php:23-33 copies those values into config('mail.mailers.smtp.password'); app/Helpers/functions.php:58-62 serves every other setting from the same cache entry.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: .env.example:31 sets CACHE_DRIVER=redis and config/database.php:129-135 makes the Redis password optional (REDIS_PASSWORD may be empty, .env.example:19-21) — any party able to read the Redis keyspace obtains live SMTP/bot/geetest credentials; the keys are also dumped in any cache:clear backup or Redis persistence file.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: config/cache.php:101 applies only an APP_NAME-derived key prefix, not encryption; there is no at-rest protection comparable to App\Casts\EncryptedOrPlaintext used for payment secrets (app/Models/Pay.php:15-19).

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Reading the cache requires network or container access to Redis, which is normally bound to the compose-internal network without published ports; Redis access is already close to full application compromise.
preconditions: attacker gains read access to the Redis instance (misconfigured exposure, weak/no password, backup leak)
findings.recommendation: Encrypt sensitive system-setting fields with the same APP_KEY-backed cast used for payment secrets, require a Redis password, and document that Redis must never be published.

findings.title: GET-based state-changing payment endpoints with fixed sleep(2) and no webserver rate limiting

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: routes/common/pay.php:28,32 exposes GET /pay/yipay/notify_url and GET /pay/vpay/notify_url; routes/common/pay.php:35-38 exposes GET stripe/check, stripe/charge, stripe/return_url; routes/common/pay.php:11-12 exposes pay-gateway redirects.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:113-118, VpayController.php:196-201, EpusdtController.php:99-105 and TokenPayController.php:100-106 sleep(2) before redirecting, with no order lookup or throttle in front of the sleep.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: conf/fpm-pool.conf:12 pm.max_children=100; an unauthenticated client issuing ~50 requests/second pins all FPM workers for the full sleep window, denying service to the storefront and to legitimate gateway notifications.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: conf/default.conf:1-66 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:1-33 define no limit_req/limit_conn zone; app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26 exempts only pay/*/notify_url and pay/*/return_url, and CSRF never applies to GET anyway.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: This is a denial-of-service class issue that requires sustained request volume; it does not leak data or complete orders without a valid signature, and an upstream WAF/CDN (not part of the repository) may absorb it.
preconditions: attacker can reach the storefront over the network
no upstream rate limiting or CDN
findings.recommendation: Add nginx limit_req/limit_conn for /pay/* and the storefront, remove or shrink the fixed sleep(2) (poll the order instead), and move notify handlers to POST where the gateway supports it.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy; HSTS and HTTPS detection depend on correct proxy trust

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php:15-22 sets nosniff/frame-options/referrer-policy/permissions-policy and conditional HSTS; no CSP is set.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: conf/default.conf:10-13 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:4-7 add the same four headers only.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Every HTML response (storefront and dcat admin); a stored-XSS primitive (e.g. SVG upload under /uploads/ or a template editor field) is not constrained by CSP.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php:20 requires $request->isSecure(); with .env.example:66 TRUSTED_PROXIES empty this is false behind a TLS-terminating proxy, so HSTS is silently skipped.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Missing CSP is a defence-in-depth gap, not an exploit; the app already escapes output through Blade and sets X-Frame-Options, and no stored-XSS sink was confirmed in this recon phase.
preconditions: existence of an injection sink elsewhere (owned by the XSS team)
findings.recommendation: Add a conservative CSP (self plus the specific third-party CDNs the admin theme loads) and document the TRUSTED_PROXIES + HSTS pairing.

findings.title: Upload directories are not PHP-executable (positive) but accept arbitrary extensions

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: config/filesystems.php:72-77 (admin disk root public_path('uploads'), visibility public) and config/admin.php:262-272 (dcat upload disk 'admin', images/ and files/ subdirectories).
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: conf/default.conf:26-45 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:10-29 wrap both /uploads/ and /storage/ in `^~` prefix locations that deny dotfiles and \.php$, then try_files $uri =404; the FastCGI block is restricted to `location ~ \.php$` (conf/default.conf:57-65).
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Files placed by an administrator are served from the application origin as static content; SVG/HTML uploads become same-origin script containers.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: No extension/MIME allow-list exists for dcat admin uploads; the only barrier is that uploading requires an authenticated administrator.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: PHP execution is denied at the webserver for both upload roots, so the classic webshell path is closed; the residual SVG/HTML storage issue requires admin credentials or an admin CSRF chain (no CSRF exception covers admin routes, app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26).
preconditions: administrator-level access to an upload form
victim opening the uploaded asset directly
findings.recommendation: Restrict admin uploads to an explicit image/document allow-list and serve /uploads/ with Content-Disposition or a separate cookie-less origin.

findings.title: Payment credentials are encrypted at rest but legacy plaintext remains readable and admin-edit placeholder handling is heuristic

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Models/Pay.php:15-19 declares the EncryptedOrPlaintext cast for merchant_id/merchant_key/merchant_pem; app/Casts/EncryptedOrPlaintext.php:17-49 decrypts only base64-JSON-with-iv/value/mac values and stores new values with Crypt::encryptString.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Casts/EncryptedOrPlaintext.php:23-25 returns any non-matching value verbatim, so pre-upgrade rows stay plaintext in the database until `php artisan pay:encrypt-secrets` runs (database/sql/upgrade-php83.sql:74-78).
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: A read-only database leak (SQL injection, backup, replica) exposes every gateway credential that has not yet been re-saved through the admin form.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: app/Admin/Controllers/PayController.php:30-32, 70-72, 110-122 mask stored secrets as ******** and :137-145 preserve the stored value when the masked placeholder is submitted.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Both the ciphertext and the plaintext require database read access; APP_KEY lives in .env, so ciphertext alone is not decryptable without further access. The residual window is bounded by whether the operator ran the documented encrypt command.
preconditions: database read primitive or backup disclosure
legacy rows not yet re-encrypted
findings.recommendation: Run pay:encrypt-secrets as part of the upgrade, surface a startup warning when any pays row is stored in plaintext, and fail closed (throw) instead of returning unencrypted values in production.

findings.title: Queue/mail failure handling records failures but never alarms, and worker log location differs per image

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: config/queue.php:16 default sync vs .env.example:36 QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis; config/queue.php:82-86 failed driver database/table failed_jobs.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Jobs/MailSend.php:23-30 (tries=2, timeout=30) with no failed() handler; exceptions bubble from Mail::send at line 71 after invalid recipients are only logged (lines 60-65).
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Order delivery is committed before any notification dispatch (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:434 then 436-452), so customers always get their carmis; operators may silently miss paid-order and delivery emails, and /tmp/work.log (Dockerfile:15) is outside stdout collection.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: database/sql/install.sql:341-353 and database/sql/upgrade-php83.sql:40-62 provision failed_jobs with the Laravel 12 uuid column, so failure recording itself works.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: This is not directly attacker-usable; it becomes security-relevant only as undetected abuse of the notification/queue path (e.g. mail-bomb retries or a stuck worker hiding fraudulent orders).
preconditions: SMTP misconfiguration or provider outage
findings.recommendation: Implement failed() handlers that alert the administrator, route worker logs to stdout, and add a `queue:monitor`/health check.

findings.title: Container runtime hardening gaps: published FPM port, root supervisord, writable app tree assumptions

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: docker-compose.yml:6-8 publishes 80 and 9000; docker-compose.yml:9-20 bind-mounts .env/install.lock/uploads with ${DATA_DIR}.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: conf/supervisord.conf:9-10 starts php-fpm as root (pool user application at conf/fpm-pool.conf:5), :19-28 nginx as root; Dockerfile:15 launches the queue worker with `su application`.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: The published 9000 mapping is inert (image pool listens on 127.0.0.1:9000, verified in webdevops/php-nginx:8.3), but the compose file invites operators to add a `listen = 9000`-style override later; there is no read_only rootfs, no no-new-privileges, no capability drop and no `user:` directive.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Dockerfile:22-28 chmods the tree 0755/0644 with only storage/bootstrap-cache/public-uploads writable, so a compromised PHP worker cannot rewrite application code.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Reaching FPM directly is currently impossible because of the loopback bind; a container escape requires an independent kernel/runtime primitive, and the app tree itself is root-owned and non-writable by the web user.
preconditions: operator modifies the FPM bind address to 0.0.0.0 while keeping the published port
or an independent container-escape primitive
findings.recommendation: Drop the 9000 port mapping from docker-compose.yml, add read_only + tmpfs + no-new-privileges + cap_drop, and run supervisord under a non-root user.

findings.title: PHP runtime is not sandboxed (no disable_functions/open_basedir) and display_errors depends on the base image

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: conf/php.ini:1-8 — expose_php=Off, cgi.fix_pathinfo=0, upload/post limits 50M, session.cookie_httponly=1; no disable_functions, no open_basedir, no display_errors.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: Observed in webdevops/php-nginx:8.3: display_errors=Off, display_startup_errors=On, allow_url_include=Off, allow_url_fopen=On, disable_functions empty, open_basedir empty.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Any PHP-level arbitrary code/read primitive can read /app/.env (world-readable 0644 root:root in a default image build), traverse the filesystem and open outbound URLs; startup errors may be rendered before the application handler takes over.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: conf/php.ini uses a fail-open posture for these directives; the only defence is APP_DEBUG=false (config/app.php:44) and the FastCGI/nginx path rules.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: These directives are post-exploitation controls; they do not create a vulnerability by themselves and the shipped image already disables display_errors and expose_php.
preconditions: an independent RCE/file-read primitive
findings.recommendation: Pin display_errors=Off and display_startup_errors=Off in conf/php.ini, add disable_functions for exec-family calls that the app does not use, and consider open_basedir=/app:/tmp.

findings.title: Stripe charge/check return raw SDK exception text and accept a missing order-context token

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:524-558 (`charge`) returns $e->getMessage() to the client at line 555; :473-522 (`check`) and :434-471 (`returnUrl`) only validate the context token when it is present (`$request->filled('context') && !validate...`).
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: Context token construction/validation lives in app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:132-168 (HMAC-SHA256 over order_sn|pay_id|amount with APP_KEY); the caller makes it optional.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Unauthenticated clients calling /pay/stripe/charge or /pay/stripe/check (routes/common/pay.php:37-38) learn Stripe API error details and can drive the endpoints with only an order_sn.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Actual order completion still requires a Stripe charge with status 'succeeded' and (for check/return) currency/amount/owner matching (StripeController.php:451-469, 500-514), so an attacker must pay real money.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Completing an order costs the attacker the order amount; the token is a hardening measure against cross-order confusion, not the only control, and Stripe errors rarely contain secrets.
preconditions: Stripe gateway configured
attacker willing to spend real funds for the order value
findings.recommendation: Require the context token unconditionally, and return a generic failure string while logging the SDK exception.

findings.title: Installer generates a fresh APP_KEY and escapes .env substitution (positive)

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:190-193 generates 'base64:'.base64_encode(Encrypter::generateKey(config('app.cipher'))) instead of reusing a shipped key; .env.example:3 leaves APP_KEY as the {app_key} placeholder only.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: HomeController:194-200 escapes backslash/quote/dollar before substitution and HomeController:138-145 rejects CRLF in every value that reaches .env.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Prevents a fleet-wide shared APP_KEY and blocks .env line injection through installer fields.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: config/app.php:124-126 keeps the key env-driven with AES-256-CBC.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Not a risk; recorded as verified good practice for the report.
findings.recommendation: Keep this behaviour; add a startup check that APP_KEY is present and non-placeholder.

findings.title: Repository hygiene for secrets: .env untracked and dockerignored, dotfiles denied (positive) with one working-copy caveat

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: .gitignore:7 ignores .env; .dockerignore:3-5 excludes .env and .env.* while keeping .env.example; `git ls-files` reports no tracked .env.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: conf/default.conf:48-50 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:32-34 deny requests matching /\.(?!well-known).*; Dockerfile-ARM64:34 deletes any baked .env.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: The real .env in this working tree exists untracked with mode 0644 root:root and is not part of any image build; no value from it was read or copied into this artifact.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Deployments that copy the checkout to a host without the container chmod step leave .env world-readable (mode observed 0644), and the installer writes .env with the process umask (HomeController:202).

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: Web access to .env is denied by both nginx configs, and file readability only matters to a local unprivileged process.
preconditions: local unprivileged access to the deployment directory
findings.recommendation: chmod 600 .env (and write it with 0600 in the installer) and document the requirement for non-container deployments.

findings.title: Admin login rate limiting and forced password change are present but scoped narrowly (informational)

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Admin/Controllers/AuthController.php:17-25 limits to 5 attempts/60s keyed by username+IP; app/Http/Middleware/ForceAdminPasswordChange.php:20-47 redirects admins whose password is exactly 'admin' to auth/setting.
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: config/admin.php:74 attaches admin.force-password to every admin route and :156-159 exempts auth/login|auth/logout from the auth middleware so the login form stays reachable.
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: Distributed credential stuffing (many IPs, one username) or a check of any non-'admin' weak password is not throttled/flagged; there is no nginx-level limiter to complement it.
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: RateLimiter::hit(...,60) is called before the attempt (line 25) and cleared on success (line 30); no lockout escalation or CAPTCHA is wired to the login form.

findings.why_it_may_not_be_necessarily_exploitabl: The limiter plus bcrypt hashing and the >=10-character installer rule make online guessing expensive; the gap needs a botnet or a weak pre-existing password.
preconditions: valid admin username known
distributed source addresses
findings.recommendation: Add an IP-independent per-account limiter with exponential backoff, and reuse the existing dcat/geetest captcha on the admin login form.

positives: Install lock is created automatically by both shipped entrypoints (Dockerfile:14, conf/start.sh:28-30) unless INSTALL=true.
Uploads and public storage are PHP-execution-denied and dotfiles are denied in both nginx variants (conf/default.conf:26-50, conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:10-34).

Payment credentials are encrypted at rest with an APP_KEY-backed cast and masked (********) in the admin grid/show/form (app/Models/Pay.php:15-19, app/Admin/Controllers/PayController.php:30-32,70-72,110-145).

CSRF exceptions are limited to gateway notify/return callbacks (app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26) and the admin panel uses the web group plus a dedicated force-password middleware (config/admin.php:74).
TRUSTED_PROXIES defaults to empty, so X-Forwarded-For cannot spoof the login rate-limit key by default (app/Http/Middleware/TrustProxies.php:19-35, .env.example:64-66).
Order fulfilment is committed before notification dispatch, so mail/push failures cannot roll back delivery (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-452).
Installer input validation blocks CRLF/.env injection and the APP_KEY is freshly generated per install (app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:138-200).

Security headers (nosniff, frame-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy, conditional HSTS) are applied both by middleware and nginx (app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php:15-22, conf/default.conf:10-13).

handoffs.reason: Default admin row and forced-password-change scope (CFG-003/CFG-016) belong with the authentication review; also confirm the dcat login/logout CSRF and remember-cookie behaviour at runtime.
CFG-002 needs a runtime proof: compute the yipay signature with the seeded placeholder key against a real pending order and observe whether completedOrder ships carmis.
CFG-005 (plaintext Redis system-setting cache) and CFG-013 (raw Stripe SDK error echo) are information-disclosure candidates.
CFG-006 (sleep(2) on GET return_url handlers with no limit_req) is a worker-exhaustion vector worth a bounded concurrency test.

uncertainties: Plaintext of the fixed bcrypt administrator hash in database/sql/install.sql:246 could not be determined; seven common candidates were rejected with password_verify() in PHP 8.3. [Needs Verification]

Whether the installer can actually write /app/.env and /app/install.lock in the Debian image depends on how the operator mounts those paths: the image tree is root-owned 0755/0644 (Dockerfile:22-28), so the application user can only write the bind-mounted .env. [Needs Verification]
Nginx nested-location PHP denial for /uploads/ and /storage/ was confirmed from configuration semantics only, not from a live request. [Needs Verification]

pm.status_path=/fpm-status and ping.path=/fpm-ping are declared (conf/fpm-pool.conf:10,20) but no nginx location routes them; the assumption that they are unreachable is based on config review, not runtime probing. [Needs Verification]
The exact webdevops FPM pool definition used by the Debian image was observed from the image, but the runtime supervisord tree (project conf/supervisord.conf is ARM64-only) was not started.
coverage_gaps: No dynamic verification of Set-Cookie flags, HSTS emission or rate-limiter behaviour (static mode).
Redis and MySQL server-level authentication were not inspected (infrastructure, not repository).
TLS termination tier is not represented in the repository, so TRUSTED_PROXIES/ADMIN_HTTPS deployment values could not be evaluated.
.env values were intentionally not read; only .env.example placeholders and file metadata were used.
